findings.title: Cutover loses its report on any unexpected exception
findings.description:
The module docstring promises that the first failure stops the run and the report is still written. `run_steps` only catches `StepFailed` and `CalledProcessError`. Several steps can raise something else:
- `step_production` runs `(ctx.main.backup_root / "backup-health.log").read_text().splitlines()[-1]`. It raises `FileNotFoundError` if the log is absent, or `IndexError` if it is empty. `run_health` guards the same read for the tick log, but this one is unguarded.
- `conf_sums()` in `cutover_227_host.py` uses `next(... for r in rows if ...)` with no default. That raises a bare `StopIteration` if `17/main` is missing from `pg_lsclusters`.
- A missing `rclone`, `sudo` or `bash` raises `FileNotFoundError` from `subprocess.run`.

In each case the traceback escapes `main()` and `report.write_text(...)` never runs. That is the failure mode where an operator needs the record most, partway through a host-mutating cutover. Convert these cases to `StepFailed` with a message, using `require` as the other steps do. Otherwise have `run_steps` record the exception on the step, as a top-level handler at a process boundary, and continue to write the report.

findings.title: Cluster names and host facts are re-spelled as literals instead of defined once
findings.description:
`TICK = "17/tick"` and `MAIN` are defined in `cutover_227_helpers.py`. The cutover still repeats the same values elsewhere:
- `CHECK_ALLOWED` and `APPLY_ALLOWED` hard-code `17/tick` inside regexes.
- `TICK_UNIT = "postgresql@17-tick"` re-encodes the cluster name.
- `RCLONE_REMOTE = "b2"` in `cutover_227_host.py` duplicates `RCLONE_REMOTE=b2` in `setup-backup.sh`.
- `HOST_BACKUP_ROOT = Path("/data/backup")` duplicates the operator-supplied `--backup-root` and the `17/main` row's `backup_root`.

This breaks the CLAUDE.md rule "changing a value should require editing exactly one place". It also undermines the stated purpose of `backup_clusters.py`, which is that no tick path is a literal in a script. Build the regexes with `re.escape(TICK)`, derive the unit name from `TICK`, and take the host root from the table or a single shared constant.

findings.title: Tick provisioning no longer creates the proof database, but the 226 proof harness still depends on it
findings.description:
The script drops `trading_tick_proof` and the `MT_PROOF_226_*` URL keys. These are still referenced elsewhere:
- `scripts/proof_226/common.py:21-22` reads `MT_PROOF_226_DB_URL` and `MT_PROOF_226_MAINTENANCE_URL`.
- `scripts/proof_226/cli.py` and `scripts/proof_226/guard.py` reference `trading_tick_proof`.
- `src/manta_trading/data/tick/constants.py:288` still defines `TICK_PROOF_DB_NAME`.

On a freshly provisioned host the harness has neither a database nor `.env` keys. The harness unit tests use fakes, so nothing flags this. If retiring the proof database is intended, remove or mark the harness and constant as retired. If not, the provisioning change is a regression. The scope of this change doesn't say which.

findings.title: Provisioning tests assert source text rather than behavior
findings.description: The new tests slice the shell script with regexes and compare strings. For example, `test_parent_directories_755_data_directory_700` compares assignment lines, and `test_roles_are_applied_with_replication` checks that a substring is present in the function body. `test_roles_sql_grants_replication_only_when_asked` only checks that `ALTER ROLE` appears before `\else`. These tests pass if the text is present even when the behavior is wrong, and they fail on harmless reformatting. The `hba_content` test is the better pattern because it executes the function. The SQL gating (`\if :{?with_replication}`) is the part that needs real execution. Run it against a throwaway database the fixture creates, which the project's database-safety rules allow.

findings.title: A test assertion is weakened by an unexplained exception
findings.description: `assert "@" not in text.replace("@192", "")` guards against unfilled placeholders but carves out `@192`. I found no `@192` or `@<digit>` anywhere under `deploy/`, so the carve-out looks like a leftover from debugging the `patsub_replacement` bug. It makes the no-placeholder check weaker for no reason. Remove it, since `test_ampersand_survives_substitution` already covers that bug.

findings.title: `b2_lifecycle.sh` output parsing in `setup-backup.sh` has an empty-output edge
findings.description: `LIFECYCLE_OUT=$(... ) || true` is followed by `done <<< "$LIFECYCLE_OUT"`. If the helper ever prints nothing, the loop reads one empty line and reports `MISSING <cluster> lifecycle-read ` with no detail. The helper also makes one `rclone backend lifecycle` call per cluster, although the rule set is bucket-wide. Neither affects correctness today.

findings.title: Cluster table parsing and cron rendering
findings.description: The shell and Python table parsers apply the same rules. Every substitution quotes its replacement, which avoids the bash 5.2 `&` problem on `2>&1`. A missing `@CLUSTER_BLOCKS@` marker, a missing `--pgdata`, an unfilled placeholder and an unescaped `%` are each refused before any output is written. Tests cover these, including the production-lines-gain-only-new-arguments invariant, checked against a real pre-227 fixture.
